narrative:
The model predicts you have a 45% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses to help you graduate.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this prediction were your lack of desire to pursue higher education, your clean record of zero past failures, and your very low weekend alcohol consumption. Surprisingly, the single most powerful reason the model expects you to fail is that you do not want to continue studying after this year. Among students who passed, every single one expressed a desire for higher education; your answer stands out as very different and strongly pulls the prediction toward failure.

Your perfect record with no previous failures and your very low weekend drinking both worked in your favor, pushing the prediction toward passing. However, these positive influences were not strong enough to overcome the much larger negative effect of not wanting to pursue further studies.

To improve your chances, you should seriously reflect on why you no longer want to continue your education and whether that view could change. Talking with a counselor about your goals and exploring what comes after school might help you either rediscover motivation or make a clearer plan that still lets you succeed this year.
